summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide a refundable tax credit for 90% of the cost of purchasing a gun safe, up to $500 ($1,000 for joint filers) every seven years, and directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report on the most effective gun safes.

scores.thoughts: This bill creates a refundable tax credit for gun safes, which effectively means the government will be spending money by reducing tax revenue and potentially issuing refunds to individuals. This is a direct increase in government outlay or reduction in revenue, making it a form of government spending.

The bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide a new refundable tax credit. While it doesn't directly raise or lower tax rates, it reduces the tax burden for individuals purchasing gun safes, which is a form of tax reduction.

By creating a new refundable tax credit, the bill will reduce government revenue or increase outlays, thereby contributing to the national debt. The bill does not include any provisions to offset this cost.
